The camera holds nearly static with a barely perceptible slow push-in toward the knuckles. Across the five seconds, the bark fingers move extremely slowly and organically, as if growing rather than flexing — each fingertip creeps a few millimeters tighter around the trunk, joints easing like swelling wood, while root tendrils on the back of the hand subtly thicken and shift. The moss clumps swell and settle, tiny leaves tremble faintly, and the fern fronds sway almost imperceptibly. A soft band of light slides slowly across the bark and moss textures from upper left toward lower right, revealing a wet sheen on the bark ridges, while dust particles drift gently and the spider silk strands sway faintly. Toward the end of the shot, the fingers ease back into the exact initial grip position, the light band slides back to its starting placement on the upper left, and the moss, ferns, dust, and camera framing return precisely to the state of <Picture 1>, forming a seamless loop with no visible cut.
